papers.title_en: Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology via Topology-Informed Graph Attention and Gene-Semantics Conditioning
papers.authors: Yuqi Cheng, Boshuai Zhang, Ziqi Zhang, Xiuwei Zhang
papers.evidence: 从H&E组织学图像预测空间转录组的深度学习模型
papers.tldr: 空间转录组可提供基因表达的空间信息但成本高，从H&E图像预测表达仍受限于单块嵌入不足、邻域聚合过平滑和基因索引输出头难以零样本泛化。TIGEM以组织拓扑与形态线索正则化图注意力，获得拓扑感知spot表示，并用基因语义调制替代基因索引头。在三个大规模数据集上取得总体SOTA，边界预测分辨率显著提升，并能预测训练中未见基因。其还提出图谱相关性GSC补充PCC/MSE评估空间模式保真度。
papers.abstract_en: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) profiles gene expression with spatial context but remains costly, motivating models that infer expression from H&E images. Existing approaches face three key limitations: (i) a single patch embedding is often insufficient: morphologically similar regions can exhibit distinct expression due to spatial context, while naive neighborhood aggregation can over-smooth boundaries; (ii) conventional fixed, gene-indexed output heads treat genes independently and cannot directly support strict zero-shot prediction for unseen genes; and (iii) common metrics under-measure spatial pattern fidelity and boundary resolution. To address these challenges, we propose TIGEM, a topology-informed, gene-conditioned framework for histology-to-ST inference. TIGEM learns topology-aware spot representations by regularizing graph attention with tissue-level topology and morphology cues to avoid cross-compartment smoothing, and uses gene semantic modulation to replace gene-indexed heads, enabling zero-shot prediction for unseen genes. We also introduce Graph Spectral Correlation (GSC) to evaluate spatial pattern fidelity and boundary resolution complement to PCC/MSE. Across three large-scale ST datasets, TIGEM achieves overall state-of-the-art performance and significantly improved boundary prediction resolution, and further demonstrates the ability to predict expression patterns for genes unseen during training, extending prior zero-shot histology-to-ST efforts with topology-aware spatial propagation and PLM-based gene conditioning.

papers.title_en: Where single-cell foundation models help: a public-data benchmark of annotation, in silico perturbation and gene regulatory inference
papers.evidence: 在计算机扰动任务上基准测试单细胞基础模型与监督扰动模型
papers.tldr: 单细胞基础模型被寄望用于注释、计算机扰动与基因调控推断，但适用边界不明。作者用公共数据和预设方案评测五款基础模型、四款新模型、CellOracle、监督扰动模型及简单基线。关键结果是：跨物种迁移中Nicheformer人→鼠肺达0.98，Geneformer V2鼠→人宏F1为0.88；种内嵌入未超主成分；81项删除测试均未达预设标准，而7/8模型的基因向量可提升敲低效应预测。基准与检查以fmaudit发布。
papers.abstract_en: Single-cell foundation models (FMs) are proposed as general tools for cell-type annotation, in silico perturbation and gene-regulatory-network inference. We benchmarked five FMs (scGPT, Geneformer V1 and V2, Nicheformer, scFoundation), four newer FMs, CellOracle, supervised perturbation models and task-matched simple baselines on public data, from Perturb-seq screens of cell lines and primary T cells to a brain organoid screen, the developing mouse cortex and lung cancer biopsies, under an analysis plan fixed before the new results. FMs helped most when labels were transferred across species: Nicheformer reached 0.98 accuracy from human to mouse lung, above every baseline (at most 0.94), and fine-tuned Geneformer V2 reached macro-F1 0.88 from mouse to human, against at most 0.74. In K562, zero-shot perturbations captured the direction of real responses (up to 76% of perturbations), Geneformer V2 tracked CRISPRa effect sizes with its overexpression protocol (rho = 0.30), and its networks recovered tumour differential expression better than co-expression. Within a species, FM embeddings did not exceed principal components. In silico deletions followed target expression and, across seven screens with replicate-level ground truth, met the predefined criterion in none of 81 tests, although in K562 and RPE1 the measured effects replicated between libraries. In contrast, the gene vectors of seven of eight FMs, including three newer models, added to expression features, predicted which knockdowns have large effects in an independent genome-wide K562 screen (rho between 0.34 and 0.44, against 0.26 with expression alone). We release the benchmark and its checks as the fmaudit package.

papers.title_en: A gene informed benchmark for BioScoring of pathology foundation models
papers.authors: Paul Vilars, Vincent Quoc-Huy Trinh, Maria Vakalopoulou, Dimitris Samaras, Stergios Christodoulidis, Mahdi S. Hosseini
papers.evidence: 将病理图像编码器与空间转录组细胞身份关联的基准
papers.tldr: 病理基础模型常靠分类、检索等下游任务比较，却难以说明编码器是否真正表征生物学。BioScore以同组织空间转录组为参考，用稀疏自编码器把图像块嵌入拆成稀疏特征并聚类，再针对52种标记基因定义的细胞身份评估特征群与表达的空间一致性。8个病理模型得分0.299–0.371，均高于3个自然图像模型的0.214–0.232，并分出三个层级。该无标签基准能定位各模型捕获或遗漏的细胞身份。
papers.abstract_en: Pathology foundation models are usually compared by their performance on downstream tasks such as classification and retrieval. While such benchmarks measure how useful a model is, they provide no insight into the biology it represents. We introduce BioScore, a benchmark that quantifies how well an image encoder captures cell identities, with spatial transcriptomics of the same tissue as the reference. A sparse autoencoder splits the encoder's patch embeddings into sparse features, which we cluster into a fixed number of groups. BioScore then measures, for each of 52 cell identities defined by marker genes, how specifically one group follows the identity's expression over the tissue. Because the autoencoder training is fully unsupervised, a match shows that the model represents the cell identity from the image alone. We score 8 pathology foundation models and 3 natural-image models. Every pathology model scores above every natural-image model (0.299--0.371 \vs 0.214--0.232), and paired tests separate three tiers among the pathology models. Unlike a supervised probe, BioScore needs no labels, builds its reference from the data and scores even from few sections, yet it ranks the encoders as a probe does. Its per-identity breakdown indicates which cell identities each encoder captures or misses.
